story: Marco Benevento grew up in Livingston, New Jersey, where he met the drummer Joe Russo in junior high and later formed the Benevento/Russo Duo. Swift, on Royal Potato Family in 2014, was named for the producer Richard Swift, whose Oregon studio hosted the sessions, and it was the first album built on Benevento's own singing. He played Pickathon in 2013 and 2014. Glera came out on Big Crown in 2026, and Russo is still a bandmate in Joe Russo's Almost Dead.
artist_reel_line: Glera came out on Big Crown in 2026, and Joe Russo, from junior high, is still a bandmate.

story: Cahalen Morrison and Eli West are a Seattle old-time and bluegrass duo, Morrison on clawhammer banjo and West on guitar. I'll Swing My Hammer With Both My Hands, their third album, came out self-released in 2014 after Our Lady of the Tall Trees, mixing originals with covers of Alice Gerrard and the Louvin Brothers, and NPR's Folk Alley praised the close country harmonies in February. They played Pickathon that year. West later went solo, and his third solo album is The Shape of a Sway; he says each record since has been about establishing himself as a solo singer of his own music.
artist_reel_line: Eli West went solo; his third solo album is The Shape of a Sway.

intro: Eric D. Johnson, between Fruit Bats.
story: Eric D. Johnson grew up around Chicago and led the indie folk band Fruit Bats, which he ended in November 2013 after a farewell show in Portland. EDJ, the self-titled album, followed on August 5, 2014 on Easy Sound, with Pickathon among his first solo shows, and KCRW called it among his most focused. He described the songs as simple stories about losses, disappointments and regrets, and also hope and perseverance. In 2015 he went back to the Fruit Bats name, with Absolute Loser in 2016 and Gold Past Life, his first for Merge, in 2019.
artist_reel_line: In 2015 he took the Fruit Bats name back, and Gold Past Life in 2019 was his first for Merge.

story: Ruban Nielson, a New Zealander and former member of The Mint Chicks, based Unknown Mortal Orchestra in Portland, and the 2011 self-titled debut won the 2012 Taite Music Prize in New Zealand. II came out February 5, 2013 on Jagjaguwar, written largely on the road, and Nielson has called it a lonely album about staying awake at night. They played Pickathon in 2014. Multi-Love followed in 2015, Sex & Food in 2018 and V in 2023, and in 2026 came Curse, a heavier EP.
artist_reel_line: Curse, a heavier EP, came out in 2026.

story: The Black Lillies formed in Knoxville in early 2009 around Cruz Contreras, formerly of Robinella and the CC Stringband. Their debut, Whiskey Angel, recorded at Contreras's own house, was named best Americana album at the Independent Music Awards, and Runaway Freeway Blues in 2013 was the breakout. They played Pickathon in 2010, 2011 and 2014. Tom Pryor and Robert Richards left in early 2015, and Hard to Please, on Thirty Tigers that October, was the first record with an outside producer, Ryan Hewitt, made at House of Blues Studio D in Nashville. Stranger to Me followed in 2018. Contreras says the key to writing Hard to Please in about two weeks was locking the door.
artist_reel_line: Contreras wrote Hard to Please in about two weeks, he says, by locking the door.

story: Destroyer is the project of the Vancouver songwriter Dan Bejar, who is also a member of The New Pornographers, and Kaputt, in 2011, was a sax-and-soft-rock breakthrough among the best reviewed albums of its year. They played Pickathon in 2014. Poison Season, on Merge on August 28, 2015, was his first album since Kaputt, and Bejar told Pitchfork he was never sure it made any sense as music, and still is not. Have We Met followed in 2020, and Dan's Boogie came out on Merge in 2025, when he toured with Father John Misty.
artist_reel_line: Dan's Boogie came out on Merge in 2025; he toured with Father John Misty.

story: Foxygen are Sam France and Jonathan Rado, who grew up in Westlake Village, California, and formed the band in 2005. We Are the 21st Century Ambassadors of Peace & Magic came out January 22, 2013 on Jagjaguwar, produced by Richard Swift, after the 2012 EP Take the Kids Off Broadway, and Fuse TV named them a must-see SXSW act that year. They played Pickathon in 2013 and 2014, the year of ...And Star Power on Jagjaguwar. Hang followed in 2017, and the duo stepped back from touring after Seeing Other People in 2019. Rado has said the band's rise as a buzz act owed a lot to the 1960s sound of that first record.
artist_reel_line: They stepped back from touring after Seeing Other People in 2019.

story: Jonathan Richman formed the Modern Lovers around Boston in 1970, at 19, with the Velvet Underground as a model, and the Sex Pistols later covered Roadrunner from the original band's 1976 album. He played Pickathon in 2014, the year of No Me Quejo de Mi Estrella, and returned in 2017. He still tours small venues with the drummer Tommy Larkins.
artist_reel_line: He still tours small venues with the drummer Tommy Larkins.
